description: Integrated Science prep for 8th grade - life, earth, physical science

questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes. Atoms are smaller but are not alive, and tissues and organs are made of many cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: every dino, from the tiniest to the T-Rex, is built from cells - life's LEGO bricks!
questions.question: Which statement best describes the basic unit of life?

questions.explanation: The cell membrane is a selective barrier that controls which substances pass in and out, keeping the cell's interior stable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the membrane is the bouncer at the dino club - it decides who gets in and who stays out!
questions.question: Which cell structure best controls what enters and leaves the cell?

questions.explanation: Mitochondria break down food molecules to release energy in a usable form, so they are called the powerhouses of the cell.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mitochondria are the dino's snack-powered batteries - munch food, make energy!
questions.question: Which organelle is best described as the energy producer of the cell?

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts capture sunlight for photosynthesis. Animal cells do not photosynthesize, so they lack chloroplasts (mitochondria, nuclei, and membranes are in both).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants are solar-powered dinos - their chloroplasts are tiny green solar panels!
questions.question: Which organelle is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?

questions.explanation: The nucleus stores DNA, the instructions for the cell. It acts as the control center directing all cell activities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the nucleus is the dino's brain-in-a-bubble - it keeps the DNA instruction manual safe!
questions.question: In which part of the cell is the genetic material held?

questions.explanation: Tissues are groups of similar cells doing the same job, like muscle tissue. Many tissues form an organ, and organs form organ systems.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cells form a tissue team, tissues build an organ, organs join the system squad!
questions.question: A group of similar cells working together is best described as a:

questions.explanation: Ribosomes read genetic instructions and link amino acids into proteins, which do most of the cell's work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ribosomes are tiny dino chefs - they follow the recipe and cook up proteins!
questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for building proteins in the cell?

questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the thick fluid inside the cell where organelles sit and where many chemical reactions happen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cytoplasm is the dino's swimming pool - all the organelles float around in it!
questions.question: What is the jelly-like substance that fills the cell and holds the organelles in place?

questions.explanation: The stiff cell wall outside the membrane supports the plant cell and helps plants stand upright without bones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the cell wall is the plant's suit of armor - stiff, strong, and holding everything up!
questions.question: Which structure best gives plant cells their rigid shape and support?

questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down waste, invaders, and old organelles for recycling.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lysosomes are the dino cleanup crew - they munch trash and recycle the leftovers!
questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for breaking down waste and worn-out cell parts?

questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus receives proteins, folds and labels them, then sends them off in vesicles like a post office.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Golgi is the dino post office - it wraps proteins in packages and ships them out!
questions.question: Which organelle packages proteins and ships them to their destinations?

questions.explanation: The large central vacuole holds water and pushes against the cell wall, keeping the plant firm. When it loses water, the plant wilts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the vacuole is the plant's water balloon - full balloon means a perky plant, flat balloon means a sad wilt!
questions.question: In plant cells, which large organelle stores water and keeps the cell firm?

questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells store their DNA inside the nucleus. (A tiny bit is also in mitochondria and chloroplasts.)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: DNA lives in the nucleus vault - the most guarded room in the cell!
questions.question: In eukaryotic cells, where is most of the DNA found?

questions.explanation: An amoeba is a single cell that carries out all life functions on its own, making it unicellular.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the amoeba is a one-dino show - a single cell doing every job all by itself!
questions.question: An amoeba is observed under a microscope as a single cell. It is best classified as what kind of organism?

questions.correctAnswer: Plant cells have both chloroplasts and mitochondria
questions.explanation: Plants need chloroplasts to capture sunlight AND mitochondria to release energy from food. Animals skip photosynthesis, so they only need mitochondria.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants double-dip on energy - solar panels AND batteries, while animals just bring batteries!
questions.question: Plant cells get energy from both photosynthesis and cellular respiration, while animal cells use only cellular respiration. What is the best conclusion from this observation?

questions.explanation: Cells group into tissues, tissues build organs, and organs work together in organ systems - each level is larger and more complex.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: think of a dino marching band - players, then sections, then the whole band, then the parade!
questions.question: Which is the correct order from smallest to largest?

questions.correctAnswer: Its surface area would be too small to supply the large volume inside
questions.explanation: As a cell grows, volume grows faster than surface area. A giant cell could not move materials in and out fast enough through its relatively small surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a cell is like a dino drive-through - if the restaurant gets huge but the window stays tiny, nobody gets fed!
questions.question: Based on the relationship between surface area and volume, why can't a single cell grow as large as a basketball?

questions.correctAnswer: Chloroplasts capture energy; mitochondria release energy
distractors: Chloroplasts make proteins; mitochondria make DNA
Mitochondria capture energy; chloroplasts release energy
Both do exactly the same job
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts trap light energy to build food (photosynthesis). Mitochondria break food down to release usable energy (cellular respiration).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: chloroplasts are the farmers growing food, mitochondria are the kitchens cooking it into energy!
questions.question: How do the jobs of chloroplasts and mitochondria differ?

questions.explanation: During interphase the cell grows and copies its DNA, so each daughter cell will get a complete set of genetic instructions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: before the dino splits into two, it photocopies the instruction manual - no copy, no split!
questions.question: Before a cell divides by mitosis, what must happen during interphase?

questions.correctAnswer: It allows some substances through but blocks others
questions.explanation: Selectively permeable means the membrane chooses: nutrients and needed materials pass in, while harmful or unneeded substances are kept out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the membrane is a picky dino bouncer with a VIP list - some molecules get in, the rest wait outside!
questions.question: The cell membrane is described as selectively permeable. What does that mean?

questions.explanation: DNA looks like a twisted ladder, called a double helix. The rungs are pairs of bases and the sides are sugar and phosphate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: DNA is a twisted dino ladder - climb up and read the rungs to find the traits!
questions.question: Which statement best describes the shape of a DNA molecule?

questions.explanation: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the instructions for one trait, such as eye color.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a gene is one recipe card in the giant dino cookbook of DNA!
questions.question: A section of DNA that codes for one trait is best defined as:

questions.explanation: Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring through genes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: heredity is why baby dinos look like their dino parents - traits get handed down!
questions.question: The passing of traits from parents to offspring is called:

questions.explanation: A dominant allele shows its trait even when only one copy is present, masking the recessive allele.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dominant allele is the loud dino - it shouts its trait even with just one copy!
questions.question: A trait that appears when only one copy of the allele is present is best described as:

questions.correctAnswer: Two copies of the recessive allele
questions.explanation: A recessive trait is hidden by a dominant allele, so it only shows when the organism has two recessive copies.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: recessive traits are shy dinos - they only come out when the loud dominant one is gone!
questions.question: For a recessive trait to appear, what must an organism have?

questions.explanation: A Punnett square is a grid that shows the possible allele combinations offspring can inherit from two parents.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a Punnett square is the dino's crystal ball for predicting baby traits!
questions.question: Which tool is used to predict the possible traits of offspring from two parents?

questions.correctAnswer: Genotype is the alleles; phenotype is the visible trait
distractors: Genotype is visible; phenotype is hidden
They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is in RNA; phenotype is in DNA
questions.explanation: Genotype is the pair of alleles an organism carries (like Tt), while phenotype is the trait you actually see (like tall).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genotype is the secret dino recipe, phenotype is the dish you see on the table!
questions.question: How do genotype and phenotype differ?

questions.correctAnswer: Homozygous has two identical alleles; heterozygous has two different alleles
distractors: Homozygous is dominant; heterozygous is recessive
questions.explanation: Homozygous (TT or tt) means both copies match. Heterozygous (Tt) means the copies differ.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: homozygous is twin dinos in matching outfits, heterozygous is twins in different outfits!
questions.question: How do homozygous and heterozygous genotypes differ?

questions.explanation: In a Tt x tt cross, half the boxes of the Punnett square are Tt (tall) and half are tt (short), so each offspring has a 50 percent chance of being tall.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flipping a dino coin - heads or tails, each baby has a fifty-fifty shot at tall!
questions.question: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over short (t). If a Tt plant crosses with a tt plant, what is the most likely chance of a tall offspring?

questions.correctAnswer: A change in the DNA sequence
questions.explanation: A mutation is any change in the DNA code. Some are harmless, some cause disease, and a few create helpful new traits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a mutation is a typo in the dino instruction manual - sometimes harmless, sometimes a superpower!
questions.question: Which statement best defines a mutation?

questions.explanation: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs - one set from each parent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 46 chromosomes, 23 pairs - the dino's complete instruction set, half from each parent!
questions.question: How many chromosomes are found in a typical human body cell?

questions.explanation: Females have two X chromosomes; males have one X and one Y. The father's sperm decides the child's sex.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: XX means a girl dino, XY means a boy dino - dad's chromosome picks the team!
questions.question: Which chromosomes determine biological sex in humans?

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction uses one parent and mitosis, so offspring are genetically identical clones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: asexual reproduction is the dino photocopier - one parent, exact copies, no mixing!
questions.question: A starfish regrows from a single arm into a whole new starfish identical to the parent. Which type of reproduction does this best describe?

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents through meiosis and fertilization, creating unique offspring.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sexual reproduction shuffles the dino deck - every baby gets a brand-new hand of genes!
questions.question: Which type of reproduction creates offspring with genetic variation from two parents?

questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine always pairs with thymine and cytosine always pairs with guanine, held by hydrogen bonds.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A hugs T, C hugs G - the dino base-pair dance partners never switch!
questions.question: Which base pairing is correct in DNA?

questions.correctAnswer: Mitosis makes 2 identical cells; meiosis makes 4 different gametes
questions.explanation: Mitosis copies a cell exactly for growth and repair. Meiosis halves the chromosomes to make gametes with new gene combinations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mitosis is the copy machine for body cells, meiosis is the shuffle machine for baby-making cells!
questions.question: What is the main difference between mitosis and meiosis?

questions.correctAnswer: Crossing over during meiosis shuffles genes
questions.explanation: During meiosis, chromosomes swap pieces (crossing over) and line up randomly, so each gamete - and each sibling - gets a unique gene mix.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: meiosis shuffles the gene deck and deals a fresh hand to every dino sibling!
questions.question: Based on genetic variation, why do siblings from the same parents look different from each other?

questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance neither allele fully wins, so the heterozygous offspring show a blended intermediate trait - pink.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red plus white paint makes pink - incomplete dominance blends the dino colors!
questions.question: In snapdragons, red (R) and white (W) show incomplete dominance. What color are RW offspring most likely to be?

questions.explanation: A Tt x Tt Punnett square has four boxes: TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Only one box (tt) shows the recessive short trait, so 1 out of 4 is 25 percent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one lucky box out of four - the short dino hides until both recessive alleles team up!
questions.question: Two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt) cross. What percent of offspring will most likely be short (tt)?

questions.correctAnswer: Mutations, crossing over, and random fertilization
questions.explanation: New gene combinations come from DNA mutations, chromosome pieces swapping in crossing over, and the random joining of gametes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: three ways to remix the dino genes - typos, swaps, and surprise pairings!
questions.question: Which three processes create genetic variation?

questions.explanation: Producers like plants make their own food through photosynthesis, forming the base of every food chain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: producers are the dino chefs - they cook food from sunlight and nobody else has to!
questions.question: An organism that makes its own food is best classified as a:

questions.explanation: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: decomposers are nature's recyclers - they turn dino leftovers back into soil snacks!
questions.question: Which type of organism breaks down dead plants and animals?

questions.explanation: Consumers cannot make their own food, so they eat producers or other consumers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: consumers are the dino diners - they show up hungry and eat what others made!
questions.question: An organism that eats other organisms for energy is best classified as a:

questions.explanation: Herbivores eat only plants. Carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both, and decomposers break down dead matter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: herbivores are the salad-loving dinos - all veggies, no meat!
questions.question: An animal that eats only plants is best classified as a:

questions.explanation: A food chain flows from producer to herbivore to carnivore: grass is eaten by the rabbit, which is eaten by the fox.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: follow the dino dinner - grass feeds the rabbit, rabbit feeds the fox, nobody eats backwards!
questions.question: Which of the following best shows a correct food chain?

questions.correctAnswer: Habitat is where it lives; niche is its role
distractors: Habitat is the role; niche is the address
questions.explanation: A habitat is an organism's address - where it lives. A niche is its job - what it eats, what eats it, and how it fits in.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: habitat is the dino's home address, niche is the dino's job description!
questions.question: How do habitat and niche differ?

questions.correctAnswer: A food web shows many connected food chains
distractors: A food web has only one chain
A food chain has more organisms
questions.explanation: Real ecosystems have overlapping feeding relationships. A food web links many food chains, showing the true complexity.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a food chain is one dino dinner line, a food web is the whole cafeteria at lunch rush!
questions.question: How is a food web different from a food chain?

questions.correctAnswer: Energy is lost as heat at each level
questions.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy moves up each level; the rest is used for life processes or lost as heat, so higher levels support fewer organisms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: energy leaks like a dino's leaky lunchbox - only a tenth makes it to the next level!
questions.question: Based on energy transfer between trophic levels, why are there fewer organisms at the top of an energy pyramid?

questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population an environment can support with its food, water, and space.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: carrying capacity is the dino hotel's max guests - no more rooms, no more dinos!
questions.question: The maximum population an environment can support is best defined as its:

questions.explanation: Wolves hunt rabbits (predator), and rabbits are hunted (prey). Their populations rise and fall together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wolves chase rabbits, rabbits dodge wolves - the classic dino chase that never ends!
questions.question: Wolves eat rabbits, and rabbit numbers affect wolf numbers. Which type of relationship does this best describe?

questions.explanation: In mutualism both species benefit - the bee gets nectar and the flower gets pollinated.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mutualism is the dino buddy system - both pals win, high-five!
questions.question: Bees get nectar from flowers while pollinating them, and both benefit. Which symbiotic relationship does this best describe?

questions.explanation: Two lions fighting over the same zebra are competing for the same limited food resource.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two dinos, one snack - may the hungriest dino win!
questions.question: Two lions fighting over the same prey is the best example of:

questions.explanation: Invasive species have no natural predators in the new area, so they spread fast and crowd out native organisms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: invasive species are uninvited dino party crashers - they eat everything and push the locals out!
questions.question: Based on ecosystem interactions, why is an invasive species harmful to an ecosystem?

questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, and respiration and decay release it back, cycling carbon through the ecosystem.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: carbon dioxide is the dino's recycled breath - plants breathe it in, animals breathe it out!
questions.question: Which gas cycles between the air, plants, and animals in the carbon cycle?

questions.explanation: Roughly 90 percent of energy is lost as heat or used by the organism, leaving about 10 percent for the next trophic level.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the 10 percent rule - the dino tax collector takes 90 percent at every level!
questions.question: Based on energy pyramids, about how much energy transfers from one trophic level to the next?

questions.explanation: Toxins concentrate as they move up the food chain because each predator eats many contaminated prey - top predators get the highest dose.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: toxins climb the dino food ladder - the top predator gets the biggest poisonous pile!
questions.question: Pollutants become more concentrated in top predators. This process is called:

questions.correctAnswer: Primary starts on bare rock; secondary starts where soil exists
questions.explanation: Primary succession begins on lifeless surfaces like lava rock and takes centuries to build soil. Secondary succession regrows after a disturbance where soil already exists.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: primary succession builds a dino city from bare rock, secondary rebuilds after the storm!
questions.question: How do primary and secondary succession differ?

questions.explanation: A limiting factor, like water in a desert, restricts how large a population can grow.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a limiting factor is the dino's empty water bowl - no water, no more dinos!
questions.question: In a desert, lack of water keeps the rabbit population small. The water is best described as a:

questions.explanation: Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as precipitation, and collects in bodies of water - then the cycle repeats.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the water cycle is the dino's endless road trip - up to the clouds, down as rain, back to the sea!
questions.question: Which is the correct order of the water cycle?

questions.explanation: A keystone species, like sea otters controlling urchins, holds the ecosystem together - remove it and the whole system collapses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the keystone species is the dino arch's center stone - pull it out and everything tumbles!
questions.question: A species whose removal would cause an ecosystem to collapse is best described as a:

questions.explanation: The three rock types are igneous (cooled magma), sedimentary (pressed layers), and metamorphic (changed by heat and pressure).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: three dino rock flavors - fire-cooled, layer-cake, and squeeze-changed!
questions.question: What are the three main types of rock?

questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when melted rock (magma or lava) cools and hardens.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: igneous rocks are born in dino fire - hot lava cools into hard stone!
questions.question: Which rock type forms from cooled magma or lava?

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form when layers of sand, mud, and shells press together over time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sedimentary rocks are layer-cake dinos - pressed flat, one tasty layer at a time!
questions.question: Which rock type forms from pressed layers of sediment?

questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks are existing rocks transformed by intense heat and pressure deep underground.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: metamorphic rocks got the dino squeeze - heat and pressure remodeled them!
questions.question: Which rock type forms when heat and pressure change an existing rock?

questions.correctAnswer: Weathering breaks rock down; erosion moves it away
distractors: Erosion breaks rock; weathering moves it
questions.explanation: Weathering cracks and crumbles rock in place. Erosion then carries the pieces away by water, wind, or ice.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: weathering is the dino hammer smashing rock, erosion is the dino truck hauling it away!
questions.question: How do weathering and erosion differ?

questions.explanation: Water evaporates into vapor, condenses into clouds, and falls back as precipitation - the endless water cycle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: up as vapor, together as clouds, down as rain - the dino water merry-go-round!
questions.question: Which three processes drive the water cycle?

questions.explanation: Earth's crust is broken into plates that drift on the hot mantle. Their collisions and separations cause earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountains.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's crust is a cracked dino eggshell - the pieces drift and crash into each other!
questions.question: According to the theory of plate tectonics, what causes continents to move?

questions.explanation: Most earthquakes strike where plates grind past, pull apart, or collide - the boundaries are the active zones.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plate boundaries are the dino wrestling ring - that's where the ground shakes!
questions.question: Based on plate boundary activity, where do most earthquakes occur?

questions.correctAnswer: Where plates pull apart or push together
questions.explanation: Magma rises where plates separate (like mid-ocean ridges) or where one plate dives under another, melting as it sinks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: volcanoes pop up where dino plates split or crash - magma just can't resist the drama!
questions.question: Based on plate tectonics, volcanoes most often form:

questions.explanation: Fossils form in the soft layers of sedimentary rock. Igneous rock's heat would destroy them, and metamorphic pressure crushes them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fossils love the sedimentary layer-cake - soft beds where dino bones can rest!
questions.question: Fossils are most commonly found in which rock type?

questions.correctAnswer: Physical weathering breaks rock; chemical weathering changes its composition
questions.explanation: Physical weathering (like freezing water cracking rock) changes size and shape. Chemical weathering (like acid rain dissolving limestone) changes what the rock is made of.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: physical weathering smashes the dino cookie, chemical weathering changes the recipe!
questions.question: How do physical and chemical weathering differ?

questions.correctAnswer: Broken-down rock mixed with decayed organisms
questions.explanation: Soil forms as weathering crumbles rock and decomposers add humus from dead organisms, creating a mix that supports plants.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: soil is the dino's crunchy granola - crumbled rock mixed with bits of old plants!
questions.question: Which statement best describes what soil is made of?

questions.correctAnswer: They redistribute heat around the planet
questions.explanation: Warm currents carry heat toward the poles and cold currents cool the tropics, shaping climates of nearby coasts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ocean currents are the planet's dino conveyor belts - hauling warm and cold water around the globe!
questions.question: How do ocean currents affect climate?

questions.explanation: The 23.5-degree tilt aims each hemisphere toward the sun for half the year (summer) and away for the other half (winter).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's tilt is the dino's lean - lean toward the sun for summer, away for winter!
questions.question: What causes the seasons on Earth?

questions.correctAnswer: Matching rock layers and fossils on different continents
questions.explanation: Identical fossils and rock sequences on continents now separated by oceans show those lands were once joined.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: matching fossils on far-apart continents are puzzle pieces - the dino map was once whole!
questions.question: Which evidence best supports the idea that continents were once joined?

questions.correctAnswer: Convergent: plates collide; divergent: plates separate; transform: plates slide past
questions.explanation: Convergent boundaries crash together (mountains, trenches), divergent pull apart (new crust), transform grind sideways (faults).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: crash, split, or slide - the three dino dance moves of plate boundaries!
questions.question: How do convergent, divergent, and transform plate boundaries differ?

questions.correctAnswer: Igneous to sedimentary to metamorphic and back, in any order
questions.explanation: Any rock can become any other: igneous weathers into sediment, sediment compacts to sedimentary rock, heat and pressure metamorphose it, melting restarts the loop.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the rock cycle is the dino's endless costume change - fire, layers, squeeze, repeat!
questions.question: Which path can a rock take through the rock cycle?

questions.correctAnswer: Greenhouse gases trap heat radiating from Earth
distractors: The sun gets hotter each year
questions.explanation: Sunlight warms the ground, which radiates heat. Greenhouse gases absorb that heat and re-emit it, warming the air like a blanket.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: greenhouse gases are Earth's dino blanket - they tuck the heat in so it can't escape!
questions.question: How does the greenhouse effect warm Earth?

questions.correctAnswer: Warm water moves east across the Pacific, shifting weather patterns
questions.explanation: During El Nino, warm Pacific water sloshes east, changing storm tracks and causing floods in some regions and droughts in others.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: El Nino is the Pacific's warm dino bath spilling east - and the weather goes wild!
questions.question: What happens during El Nino?

questions.correctAnswer: Relative dating compares layers; absolute dating gives an actual age
distractors: Relative uses clocks; absolute uses fossils
questions.explanation: Relative dating orders events (this layer is older than that one). Absolute dating uses radioactive decay to assign a number of years.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: relative dating lines up the dino photo album, absolute dating stamps each photo with a year!
questions.question: How do relative and absolute dating of rocks differ?

questions.explanation: A force is any push or pull that can change an object's motion - kicking a ball pushes it, gravity pulls it down.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: forces are dino shoves and tugs - push it, pull it, make it move!
questions.question: Which statement best defines a force?

questions.explanation: Newton's first law: objects keep doing what they are doing unless a force acts. Inertia is why passengers lurch forward when a car stops suddenly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: inertia is the lazy dino - it keeps napping or keeps running until something makes it change!
questions.question: An object at rest stays at rest unless a force acts on it. Which principle does this best describe?

questions.explanation: Newton's second law: a bigger force or a smaller mass gives more acceleration - pushing a light wagon is easier than pushing a heavy truck.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: F = ma - the dino's pushing recipe: heavy things need a bigger shove to get moving!
questions.question: Which equation represents Newton's second law of motion?

questions.correctAnswer: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
distractors: Objects at rest stay at rest
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: when you push on something, it pushes back just as hard - like a rocket pushing gas down and the gas pushing the rocket up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: push the dino and the dino pushes back - every shove gets an equal shove in return!
questions.question: Which statement best describes Newton's third law of motion?

questions.explanation: Speed tells how fast something moves: divide the distance traveled by the time it took.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: speed is the dino's race math - miles divided by hours tells you how fast those legs moved!
questions.question: Which formula is used to calculate speed?

questions.explanation: Friction is the force that resists sliding between surfaces - it lets shoes grip the floor but slows a rolling ball.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: friction is the dino's invisible handbrake - it grabs sliding things and slows them down!
questions.question: Which force opposes motion between two touching surfaces?

questions.explanation: Gravity pulls everything toward Earth's center, which is why dropped objects fall down.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: gravity is Earth's dino hug - it pulls everything in tight toward the middle!
questions.question: In which direction does gravity pull objects on Earth?

questions.correctAnswer: Kinetic is energy of motion; potential is stored energy
distractors: Kinetic is stored; potential is motion
questions.explanation: A rolling ball has kinetic energy. A ball held at the top of a hill has potential energy waiting to be released.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: kinetic energy is the running dino, potential energy is the dino crouched at the top of the slide!
questions.question: How do kinetic and potential energy differ?

questions.correctAnswer: It changes form but the total stays the same
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved: a falling ball's potential energy becomes kinetic energy, and the total never changes - it just switches forms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: energy is the dino's shape-shifter - it changes costumes but never leaves the party!
questions.question: What happens to energy in a closed system?

questions.explanation: A lever trades distance for force: a long handle lets a small effort lift a heavy load, giving mechanical advantage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a lever is the dino's cheat code - a long stick turns a tiny push into a giant lift!
questions.question: A crowbar lets a person lift a heavy rock with little effort. Which principle best explains this?

questions.explanation: Work is done when a force moves something: pushing a box 2 meters with 10 newtons of force does 20 joules of work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: no move, no work - the dino only earns work points when the force actually pushes something somewhere!
questions.question: Which formula is used to calculate work?

questions.correctAnswer: The rate at which velocity changes
questions.explanation: Acceleration measures how quickly velocity changes - speeding up, slowing down, or turning all count.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: acceleration is the dino's pedal - step on it to speed up, ease off to slow down!
questions.question: Which statement best defines acceleration?

questions.explanation: Atoms contain protons and neutrons in the nucleus, with electrons orbiting around them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the atom is the dino's solar system - heavy nucleus in the middle, speedy electrons zooming around!
questions.question: What are the three main particles of an atom?

questions.correctAnswer: An element has one type of atom; a compound has two or more bonded types
questions.explanation: Oxygen (O2) is an element - one atom type. Water (H2O) is a compound - hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: an element is a solo dino singer, a compound is the whole dino band playing together!
questions.question: How does an element differ from a compound?

questions.explanation: The periodic table orders elements by atomic number (proton count), grouping elements with similar properties in columns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the periodic table is the dino's seating chart - elements sit by proton number with their chemical cousins!
questions.question: How are elements arranged on the periodic table?

questions.correctAnswer: A chemical change forms a new substance; a physical change does not
questions.explanation: Melting ice is physical - still water. Burning wood is chemical - it becomes ash, smoke, and gases, brand-new substances.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: melt the dino ice cube and it's still water, but burn the dino toast and it's gone forever!
questions.question: How do chemical and physical changes differ?

questions.correctAnswer: pH below 7 is acidic; above 7 is basic
distractors: Acids and bases have the same pH
questions.explanation: The pH scale runs 0 to 14. Below 7 means acidic (like lemon juice), above 7 means basic (like soap), and 7 is neutral.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the pH scale is the dino's sour-to-soapy meter - low numbers pucker, high numbers feel slippery!
questions.question: How does the pH scale identify acids and bases?

questions.correctAnswer: The total mass stays the same
questions.explanation: Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed, in a chemical reaction - so the mass of the products always equals the mass of the reactants.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: atoms are dino LEGO bricks - you can rebuild them into new shapes but you never lose a single brick!
questions.question: In a sealed container, what happens to total mass during a chemical reaction?

questions.correctAnswer: Their electrons move freely between atoms
questions.explanation: Metals conduct electricity and heat because their outer electrons flow freely through the metal, carrying energy along.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: metal electrons are speedy dino messengers - they zip through the metal delivering electricity!
questions.question: Based on atomic structure, why do metals conduct electricity well?

questions.correctAnswer: Gas particles spread far apart and move freely; solid particles vibrate in fixed positions
distractors: Solids have no particles at all
questions.explanation: In a solid, particles lock in place and only vibrate. In a gas, particles fly freely and spread out to fill any container.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: solid dinos stand frozen in formation, gas dinos run wild and fill the whole room!
questions.question: Based on particle motion, why does a gas fill its container while a solid keeps its own shape?

title: Integrated Science 8
